# Charting the patient's actual path

Someone finally walked the route a patient actually takes, door to door, rather than the route the intake form assumes. The assumed path is home, clinic, referral, hospital, follow-up, done. The actual path, for the six patients shadowed this month, involved at least one detour every time: a wait for a relative to be free to travel with them, a market day that could not be missed because it is the only paid work that week, a second opinion sought from a trusted elder before committing to the hospital trip.

None of these detours are irrational once you see them from the patient's side; they are the patient solving a harder problem than "get to the hospital," which is closer to "get to the hospital without losing the week's income, without traveling alone, and without abandoning a source of advice the family already trusts." The clinic's own process was designed around the assumed path, so every one of these ordinary detours reads to the system as noncompliance rather than as the patient doing exactly what a reasonable person in that position would do.
